title: Great earthquakes in the ISC bulletin: nine named ones (Rayleigh arrivals for the radius, P / first arrivals for our relocation, the P shadow zone) and every shallow Mw >= 7.0 of 2000-2023 for the pooled syntheses

radius_enters_via.how: angles from the published epicentre and station coordinates, then the surface-wave speeds the tab uses were established with distances measured on the globe
Natural Earth land polygons, drawn in degrees on the globe

verdict_rule: A reconstructed radius 60-100% off, the error a flat map's distances would need; the real arrivals land within a few percent. Pooled: one flat map, with the same free parameters, fitting the pooled P times or the pooled shadow as well as the globe.
license_note: ISC On-line Bulletin: free with the citation International Seismological Centre, On-line Bulletin, https://doi.org/10.31905/D808B830. Natural Earth: public domain.

sources.cite: International Seismological Centre, On-line Bulletin (ISF2 phase data)
Natural Earth, 1:50m land polygons (ne_50m_land), public domain

units.distance_deg: degrees of arc (great circle from the published coordinates)
units.travel_time_s: s, arrival minus origin, median across agencies
units.ocean_frac: fraction of the great-circle path over sea (0..1)

inputs.origin: Our list of the nine named earthquakes (one entry each).
ISC On-line Bulletin, ISF2 phase data of each named earthquake (fog fetch seis-radius).
inputs.caveats: Phase names (P, Pdif, PKP, LR) are the ISC's, given by comparing with its travel-time tables.

inputs.origin: ISC catalogue query of tools/internal/build/seisbulk/fetch.go: reviewed bulletin, 2000-2023, depth ≤ 70 km, GCMT Mw ≥ 7.0.
ISC On-line Bulletin, ISF2 of each earthquake of the catalogue query, fetched one by one.

notes: Edit events.json only (one entry per earthquake), then fog fetch seis-radius (ISC query; Natural Earth once), fog lock seis-radius, fog build seis-radius. Until 2026-10-14 the land polygons were downloaded afresh at every run, from the branch head; they are now an input with a hash. The same bulletins feed fog build seis-relocate: earthquakes relocated from arrival times and station angles only (epic18). The pooled syntheses (fog build seis-bulk, 2026-10-29) use every earthquake the ISC catalogue query of tools/internal/build/seisbulk/fetch.go returns: reviewed ISC Bulletin, 2000-01-01 to 2023-12-31, depth <= 70 km, GCMT Mw >= 7.0 (264 events), then at least 50 P stations 25-95 degrees from our own centre; bulletins by event id in bulk/raw/ (gitignored, fog fetch seis-radius). The nine named earthquakes that meet the rule are counted there again, processed like the others.
